Who really built Baku's Maiden Tower? Legends and history tell very different stories.
Legend says a princess, forced to marry a man she didn't love, asked for a tall tower, then leapt from its top. Another tells of a fiery-haired girl who saved the city from a siege.

History is less certain. A Kufic inscription on the wall names Masud ibn Davud and points to the twelfth century. But some scholars argue its roots are far older, maybe even a Zoroastrian fire temple.
Inside, there's a well twenty-one meters deep. And its long buttress faces east, toward the sunrise.
